title: FounderGate Checker Reliability Scorecard
description: A machine-readable scorecard describing how RELIABLE a checker (an advisor/reviewer/auditor lane) is at its own job, measured over a labelled sample of review episodes. This is orthogonal to H11 (which scores the WRITER lane's process): H34 turns the QUESTION 'can we trust this reviewer?' into one number, a band, and an anti-trust VETO layer so a checker cannot look reliable by getting the cheap metrics right while missing real defects or flapping its verdict. Additive harness data only; never an application runtime capability, never a provider, never network. The scorer (score.mjs) is the source of truth for weights and sub-score curves; this schema only constrains shape.

schema_version.description: Semver of the scorecard schema this object targets.

checker_id.description: The checker under measurement (e.g. an advisor-verdict producer, a Copilot review pass, a proof-verifier lane).

episodes.description: Number of review episodes the metrics were measured over. A tiny sample is flagged (see LOW_SAMPLE warning) because a rate over few episodes is not yet trustworthy.

labelled_defects.description: Number of episodes that carried a GROUND-TRUTH real defect the checker was supposed to catch. miss_rate is undefined if this is 0 (see the schema-independent scorer note).

head_sha.description: Exact commit the scorecard binds to (7-40 lowercase hex). No SHA => not machine-trustable.

label.description: 'real' = metrics derived from a genuine measured checker sample with a checkable evidence_ref per episode. 'illustrative' = a shape/edge-case demo, never presented as a real measured reliability result. The H34 fixtures shipped in this repo are ALL 'illustrative' — no real checker sample has been measured yet (see the doc).

notes.description: Free-text provenance: how each raw metric was measured (which episodes, what the ground-truth labelling source was, how latency was clocked).

false_positive_rate.description: Fraction (0..1) of the checker's raised findings/blocks that were SPURIOUS (flagged a clean lane, or a finding that no one accepted). A checker that cries wolf trains reviewers to ignore it. Lower is better.

miss_rate.description: Fraction (0..1) of GROUND-TRUTH labelled defects the checker FAILED to catch (a real breach/bug it passed as clean). This is the gravest checker failure and is weighted and vetoed hardest. Lower is better.

loop_count.description: Mean review rounds the checker drove per episode before a stable verdict (rework churn the checker caused). Fewer is better; a pathological loop trips a veto.

review_latency.description: Median wall-clock SECONDS from review-request to the checker's verdict. Slower review delays every downstream lane. Lower is better.

verdict_stability.description: Does the checker give the SAME verdict on re-run of the same input? 'deterministic' = always identical; 'mostly_stable' = rare drift; 'flapping' = nondeterministic PASS/FAIL flips, which makes the verdict untrustable and trips a veto.
